blog_outline.title: Which launch monitor fits your garage: a room-depth and budget guide (with the subscription costs nobody prints)
sections: Start with a tape measure, not a budget: the three placements (behind the ball, beside the ball, on the ceiling) and what each one does to your room depth
The 10 ft rule: why every maker and forum agrees on 10 ft from ball to screen, and why radar units add 5 to 10 ft behind you on top

Under 16 ft deep: the camera and overhead shortlist (Square Home and Omni, SkyTrak ST MAX, Bushnell Launch Pro, GC3, Garmin R50, Uneekor EYE MINI LITE, ProTee VX, EYE XR and XO2, Trackman iO) with the placement distance for each
16 to 21 ft deep: when radar makes sense (Garmin R10, Rapsodo MLM2PRO and MLM2XPRO, Mevo Gen2, Full Swing KIT) and the one radar unit that fits 13 ft (SC4 Pro)
Ceiling height is the second wall: 9 ft for a driver, 9 ft 4 in to 10 ft for overhead units, and what the forums say about 7 ft 6 in rooms
Spin is the real difference between tiers: measured vs calculated, and why marked balls (RPT, Square, RCT) and metal stickers exist

The subscription table nobody prints: GSPro $250 a year plus Foresight+ Gold $599, Uneekor Pro $199, Rapsodo Core $199.99, SkyTrak Core $299.99, Trackman TPS $700; the units with no maker fee (Square, Mevo Gen2, Garmin, ProTee VX); E6 at $300 or $600 a year or $1,000 for life; Awesome Golf at $159.99 a year or $349.99 for life
Three-year cost of ownership by budget: $500, $1,000, $2,000, $3,000, $6,000 and $14,000 builds with hardware plus software added up
What the forums argue about: MLM2PRO disconnects, SkyTrak's closed ecosystem and the OpenSky bridge, the Launch Pro Gold tax, Square's driver spin axis, radar putting under 6 ft

What changed in 2026: GC3 at $3,999 on sale, EYE MINI cut to $2,999, ST MAX at $1,695, Mevo+ and SkyTrak+ discontinued, MLM2XPRO launched with putting, Square Omni backordered, Rapsodo's CLMPRO overhead on the way
Buying used: GC2 and Launch Pro refurbs, serial and battery questions, and which subscriptions follow the unit
The decision grid: room depth across the top, budget down the side, one or two units in each cell, and the enclosure that goes with it
